boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Hendrix traditions, from white-shirt dance routines and a lucky cafeteria tray to student-led philanthropy and candlelit choral services.

cards.title: Dance in Shirttails
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week’s residence-hall dance contest
cards.notes: Bring the prescribed white Oxford, tie, shorts or boxers, and tennis shoes; new students rehearse with their residence halls before the contest.
cards.short_summary: A football-victory parade evolved into Hendrix’s century-old Welcome Week dance competition.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix documents Shirttails as a residence-hall dance contest held at the end of Welcome Week; its history dates to a 1913 football victory over Ole Miss.
cards.access_notes: Participation is open to every new student, including transfers; upperclass students may enter the separate sophomore-versus-junior contest.

cards.title: Raise Funds with Campus Kitty
cards.subtitle: Student-run philanthropy with a feline-free name
cards.notes: Join a fundraiser, volunteer behind the scenes, or follow the student committee’s announcements to support its selected Conway-area nonprofits.
cards.short_summary: The oddly named student organization has organized charitable events at Hendrix since 1949.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix identifies Campus Kitty as a student-organized fundraising tradition begun as “Kampus Kitty” in 1949 and supporting local community groups.
cards.access_notes: Events and beneficiaries vary by academic year; consult current Campus Kitty announcements before participating.

cards.title: See the Ms. Hendrix Finale
cards.subtitle: Campus Kitty’s annual auditorium pageant
cards.notes: Watch for the Campus Kitty calendar and secure a ticket early; the 2024 event filled all 816 seats in Staples Auditorium.
cards.short_summary: Campus Kitty’s culminating pageant combines student performance with the College’s charitable campaign.
cards.evidence_claim: A 2024 Hendrix report calls Ms. Hendrix an annual event and one of Campus Kitty’s two largest fundraisers, noting its first sellout in March 2024.
cards.source_title: Hendrix Students’ Campus Kitty Fundraising for Nonprofits Tops $25,000 for 2023-24 Academic Year
cards.access_notes: Ticketing, date, and audience rules can change annually; verify the current Campus Kitty schedule before attending.

cards.title: Hear the Cafeteria Birthday Song
cards.subtitle: A lighted cake and Hendrix dining sing-along
cards.notes: If a birthday song starts during your meal, make room for the cafeteria crew and its lighted cake, then join the Hendrix-specific chorus.
cards.short_summary: Dining staff turn student birthdays into a communal cafeteria performance.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix Dining Services says its cafeteria crew rushes into the dining hall with a lighted cake and sings “Happy, Happy Birthday” whenever a birthday occurs.
cards.access_notes: This tradition occurs inside the campus cafeteria and is tied to student dining access and birthday scheduling.

cards.title: Spot the Lucky Disco Tray
cards.subtitle: The Caf’s elusive sparkly tray
cards.notes: Scan the cafeteria tray stack for the sparkly version; Hendrix describes finding and using the disco tray as a promise of good luck that day.
cards.short_summary: A glittering cafeteria tray carries its own Hendrix good-luck superstition.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix calls the disco tray a cafeteria tradition and states that picking up the sparkly tray brings good luck for the day.
cards.access_notes: The tray is encountered in the Hendrix cafeteria; ordinary dining-access requirements apply.

cards.title: Decode a Cafeteria Theme Day
cards.subtitle: Monthly meals built around changing motifs
cards.notes: Check dining announcements before lunch, then look for the menu and décor tied to themes such as Rock N’ Roll Day or Wiener Day.
cards.short_summary: Hendrix dining periodically remakes lunch around playful historical, holiday, or food themes.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix documents informal cafeteria “theme days,” including Rock N’ Roll Day with a live band and Wiener Day with multiple hot-dog variations.
cards.access_notes: Themes and dates vary; attendance occurs during cafeteria lunch service and follows normal dining-access rules.

cards.title: Catch Sundae Thursday
cards.subtitle: A weekly Hendrix cafeteria lunch tradition
cards.notes: Check the current dining schedule, then visit the cafeteria at Thursday lunch to see how the recurring sundae ritual fits into the day’s service.
cards.short_summary: Thursday lunch has a named weekly tradition of its own in the Hendrix cafeteria.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Hendrix Dining Services page explicitly identifies Sundae Thursday as a weekly lunch tradition.
cards.access_notes: Offered during Thursday lunch subject to the current dining calendar and ordinary cafeteria-access requirements.

cards.title: Enter Greene Chapel by Candlelight
cards.subtitle: Hendrix Choir’s six-decade winter service
cards.notes: Reserve a campus service when bookings open, or use the livestream or regional-tour listings when Greene Chapel seats are unavailable.
cards.short_summary: Choir, scripture lessons, and handheld candles transform Greene Chapel during Hendrix’s winter observance.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix describes Candlelight Carol Services as a tradition spanning more than six decades, modeled on the Festival of Nine Lessons and Carols and performed by the College Choir.
cards.source_title: Hendrix College Choir Candlelight Carol Services Set for Dec. 4-7, 17-18; Tour Stops in Russellville, Little Rock
cards.access_notes: Dates change annually, and Greene Chapel performances may require reservations; verify the current Candlelight page before attending.

cards.title: Receive the Formal Hendrix Welcome
cards.subtitle: Orientation’s class-and-family convocation
cards.notes: New students should follow the Orientation schedule to the listed venue; families and supporters are expressly invited to share the formal welcome.
cards.short_summary: The incoming class begins its Hendrix story together at a formal campus ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix’s 2025 orientation schedule explicitly calls New Student Convocation a campus tradition serving as the formal welcome for the incoming class and families.
cards.source_title: Hendrix College Class of ’29 Orientation: Move-in Day Schedule
cards.access_notes: Designed for incoming students and their families or supporters; consult the current class’s orientation schedule for venue and time.

cards.title: Take Part in Red Light Revue
cards.subtitle: A student-produced Campus Kitty event
cards.notes: Follow Campus Kitty’s annual event notices to attend or help produce the revue; the student committee controls the format and schedule.
cards.short_summary: The named revue is one of the student-built events within Hendrix’s long-running charitable campaign.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix’s official traditions page identifies Red Light Revue as a Campus Kitty event planned, organized, and executed entirely by students.
cards.access_notes: Programming and access conditions vary by Campus Kitty cycle; confirm current student-organizer announcements before attending.
